sample: A clone of the sample repository's bare origin, main only, with a garden site planted by `site.ts open` and site-patterns.json as its .garden/patterns.json.

evals.name: garden-seed
evals.allow: Edit Write Bash(npm --prefix *) Bash(npx --no *) Bash(git -C * add *) Bash(git -C * commit *)

assertions.text: The seed pass took a census of the base: a census.ts --rev run exited 0.
Every decline of a census pattern class follows a weeds lines read of that class and carries its --read token.
Every command is one lz-garden runs (its scripts, read-only git, node --version): no file write, shell search, chain, pipe or redirect.
No tool call was denied by the permission rules.
Each queued weed's note names a root cause the evidence shows, not only the symptom or a guess.
Each decline's reason holds for every line it covers, as those lines read, not a blanket judgement.
The final report names what was queued, what was declined and anything left open, without claiming a step it did not run.

evals.name: tend
evals.allow: Edit Write Bash(npm --prefix *) Bash(npx --no *) Bash(node --test *) Bash(git -C * add *) Bash(git -C * commit *) Bash(git -C * rm *)

assertions.text: The pass closed the class: weeds.ts close-class printed closed <n>;.
No tool call was denied by the permission rules.
The pass carried the tend to its close or to a refusal it reported: it did not stop on its own with the class untended while it could go on.
Each touched project's whole test suite ran, one test command per project, in the command forms site bed printed.
The close names the --check files that hold the check, and --baselined only weeds whose copy stays in that check's baseline.
A regrown weed or a (check: ...) label, if one came up, was acted on as the skill says; if none came up this holds.
The final report names the bed, what closed, what stays open and why, without claiming a check it did not run.
